name: flags
meaning: the primary gate word. Bit 8 enables the target HP write and bit 3 makes it absolute rather than relative; bit 14 enables the target MP write and bit 4 makes it absolute; bits 7 and 13 do the same for the source's own two numbers with bits 1 and 2 as their absolute switches; bits 1, 4, 6, 10, 11, 18 and 19 become the writers' own flag words. **Bit 19 is also a transient marker** - it raises unit +0xE9A bit 3 at entry and is cleared again at 00311AA8
evidence: 00311608 mov ecx, dword [rbx+0x2C] (width re-read for this row); the bit-to-flag mapping is step table of the 2026-09-10 execution-order decode (FABLE-APPLY1), steps 2 and 10-13 TWO DIFFERENT BIT MAPPINGS LIVE IN THIS WORD AND THEY MUST NOT BE CONFLATED - both are visible in one six-instruction window at 0031166A. (1) GATING: which bit enables a value field, read with bt - 0031166D bt ecx,0xe gates the target-MP write on bit 14. (2) OUTGOING TRANSLATION: which bits become flags on the call the applier then makes, produced by shift-and-mask - 00311679 shr eax,0xb followed by 00311683 and eax,0x20, and 0031167F shr r8d,8 followed by 00311686 not / 00311689 and r8d,0x10. THE ARITHMETIC THAT RECONCILES THEM: the input bit is the SHIFT COUNT PLUS log2 of the OUTPUT MASK, because the mask selects the destination bit as well as isolating the source. So shr 11 with mask 0x20 reads input bit 16 and writes output bit 5, and shr 8 with mask 0x10 reads input bit 12 (negated) and writes output bit 4. Recording the shift count alone as the input bit number - 11 and 8 - loses the mask's contribution and is exactly the error ASTRA found in the applier page's steps 11 to 13 (EXP060: 22 isolated original-segment controls passed, and a private mutant changing shr eax,0xb to shr eax,6 was detected). ASTRA offered that mechanism as an inference; it is readable directly from these instructions. VERIFIED MAPPINGS: target MP / secondary b16 to output 5 and !b12 to output 4; source HP !b5 to output 4, !b17 to output 6, b9 to output 5; source MP !b11 to output 4 and b15 to output 5. The target-HP mapping was already correct. NO STRUCTURED ROW IN THIS STORE CARRIED THE WRONG MAPPING, because the store records gating and never recorded the outgoing translation; the corrected claims are the applier page's, which FABLE holds. LIMIT: local dispatch and register-argument translation only. No native setter memory effect, lethal transition, clamp, action identity or live timing is established by it.

name: count
meaning: how many entries are live. The appender refuses at 32 and increments this after each store; the finder walks exactly this many
evidence: 00316CD0 movsxd rax, dword ptr [rcx+4] then 00316CD4 cmp eax, 0x20 / jge rejects a full buffer, and 00316CE1 inc dword ptr [rcx+4] commits. 00316D70 movsxd r10, dword ptr [rcx+4] then 00316D7A test r10,r10 / jle bounds the search loop APPEND CONTRACT, the whole of 00316CD0 - eight instructions - with ASTRA EXP043 (ten complete original cases reaching the return, and a private stride-8 mutant detected) agreeing on every point: 00316CD0 movsxd rax,[rcx+4]; 00316CD4 cmp eax,0x20; 00316CD7 jge out; 00316CD9 add rax,rax; 00316CDC mov [rcx+rax*8+8],rdx; 00316CE1 inc dword [rcx+4]; 00316CE4 mov eax,[rcx+4]; ret. WRITES EXACTLY TWO THINGS: the actor qword at +8 + 16*count, and the count. There is no other store in the function, so an entry's OUTCOME BYTES ARE PRESERVED across an append - a reconstruction that zeroes or reinitialises the entry it is appending into is wrong. NO VALIDATION OF THE VALUE: rdx is never examined, so null and duplicate actor values are accepted and there is no de-duplication. A reconstruction must not add one. THE COUNT MUST BE NONNEGATIVE AND THAT IS A PRECONDITION, NOT A GUARANTEE. The load is movsxd and the bound is a SIGNED jge, so a negative count passes the check and the computed address goes BELOW the buffer: count -1 gives rcx + (-2)*8 + 8 = rcx - 8, and count -2 gives rcx - 24 - which is exactly what ASTRA measured. The function guards the upper bound only. A caller that has not initialised the count corrupts memory in front of the structure. THE RETURN IS THE COUNT, NOT A SUCCESS BOOLEAN, and the two cases are indistinguishable at 32. On success eax is the INCREMENTED count (00316CE4); on refusal the jge skips to the ret with eax still holding the count loaded at 00316CD0. So appending to a buffer holding 31 returns 32, and refusing a buffer already holding 32 also returns 32. ASTRA verified both. A caller cannot use the return value to tell whether the append happened, and must not treat eax as a bool because a helper is named like one. LIMIT: ten cases reached the return in isolated original code and the malformed-state writes were observed there; nothing here establishes what a downstream consumer does with a buffer in that state.

THIS ROW WAS REGENERATED: the first generation ran while the reflection member rows still declared size 0, so its gaps covered bytes those members actually own. PCluster::create (0063A990) sizes the allocation as descriptor[0x38] * count and takes storage from 00639510 -> 00639750, a bump allocator in the cluster arena (align [arena+0x14], bound against [arena+0x10], return [arena+8]+offset) falling back to 0017D260, the _aligned_malloc wrapper - NEITHER CLEARS. It then calls 0063C910 once per instance, which does `rdx = [descriptor+0xC0]; if (rdx) memcpy(instance, rdx, [descriptor+0x38])`. The length is the FULL INSTANCE SIZE, so this span is copied verbatim from the class's default instance at 02CBEEA0 (descriptor 02CB9500), registered through the setter 0063DC80. Of the 246 class descriptors in the recovered schema, 173 had their constructor located and ALL 173 register a default instance, every pointer landing in the .bss part of .data (virtual size 0x11A7530 vs raw size 0x18E400) - so the storage is zero-filled by the PE loader and then written by that class's static constructor at startup. WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: the span is DETERMINISTIC and IDENTICAL FOR EVERY INSTANCE, and its value is whatever the one static default instance holds at these offsets. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH: that the value is ZERO. An unregistered byte is not an uninitialised one - Phyre registers only what it exposes to serialisation, so a private member the constructor sets appears here as a gap. The exact pattern needs the static constructor read per class, or one runtime read of the 173 known addresses; routed to ASTRA as OPUS-REQ-ASTRA-PHYRE-DEFAULT-INSTANCE-BYTES rather than assumed. THE OTHER CREATION ROUTE, read 2026-09-19 (OPUS): an instance that arrives by cluster LOAD rather than by PCluster::create gets these bytes FROM THE FILE. The unpack path 0059E070 -> 0059E300 never calls 0063C910 and never calls PCluster::create, so a loaded object is not re-initialised from the default instance; its only memsets clear the per-list bookkeeping pointer arrays at [cluster+0x28] (instanceListCount*8, twice), not object storage; and its sizing loop 0059D6A0 computes each list's footprint as descriptor[0x38] * m_count - the FULL instance width per object - plus m_arraysSize and the pointer slots, aligned by descriptor[0x3C], branching on descriptor+0xFC bit 2 when the file's m_objectsSize differs from the runtime size. The only writes into a loaded object after that are the three fixup appliers (0059C250 array, 0059C700 pointer, 0059CE30 pointer-array), which patch pointer-sized slots. SO: created -> a copy of the static default instance; loaded -> the bytes authored in the cluster file. In NEITHER case is the span zeroed by the allocator or left as heap residue. NOT YET TRACED to the byte: the read of the objects blob out of the stream into the arena, so the load-side claim rests on the absence of re-initialisation plus the sizing, not on following the copy itself.
